newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ESSEX FRUSTRATED BY NORTHANTS' CURRAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ESSEX FRUSTRATED BY NORTHANTS' CURRAN.

text.p: Essex's hopes of making ground at the top of English cricket's county championship faded on Thursday when they continued to struggle against lowly Northamptonshire on the second day of their four-day match.
Northants' Kevin Curran produced his best championship bowling performance for four years to earn his county a first-innings lead of 89 over second-placed Essex at Northampton.
Curran picked up four for 32 to restrict Essex to 275 all out in reply to the home side's 364.
By the close, Northants had stretched their lead to 103 as Russell Warren and David Roberts survived 11 tricky overs for 14 runs.
Darren Lehmann and Bradley Parker put Yorkshire on the verge of a convincing victory over Durham at Scarborough.
Australian Lehmann hit 86 and an unbeaten 74 from Parker helped Yorkshire to 372 all out and a first-innings lead of 220.
Durham then collapsed to 61 for five in the face of a hostile seam attack.
Derbyshire's former skipper, Kim Barnett, hit his second half-century of the match, but it is unlikely to save his county from a heavy defeat by Gloucestershire at Cheltenham.
The veteran batsman is 51 not out as Derbyshire showed more resolution in their second innings on 174 for three than they did in their first when all out for 120, of which Barnett contributed 58.
Derbyshire trail by 190 runs after Tasmanian Shaun Young smashed a career-best 237 out of Gloucestershire's first-innings total of 484.
Young and captain Mark Alleyne put on 244 for the fifth wicket, before Alleyne was out for 97 when the pair were within 18 runs of a county record that has stood for 121 years.
Lancashire moved a step closer to three successive championship victories when they fired out Sussex's top order at Old Trafford.
Mike Watkinson hit 75 and Ian Austin remained unbeaten on 77 as Lancashire piled up 561 for eight declared.
Then Peter Martin and Austin grabbed two wickets apiece to send the visitors sliding to 156 for five, still 256 short of avoiding the follow-on.
Sussex banked on Neil Taylor to see them through to the close, but he was out for 82.
Kent captain Steve Marsh was left two short of a century against Leicestershire at Canterbury when heavy rain washed out play for the day after lunch with Kent on 498 for nine.
However, the rain held off long enough for England all-rounder Mark Ealham, 96 overnight, to make a career-best 139.
